reason: Conversation 1 asked the right diagnostic questions (display level, glow, codes, lock), kept the diagnosis honestly open between a burnt-out element/limiter and the zone's board relay, explained how to find the full ZHRN model and PNC before any part is ordered, and steered toward an engineer while hedging the multimeter notes behind breaker isolation and 'competent' caveats. Conversation 2 was safe and correctly escalated to an engineer, but its opener was generic child-lock/induction boilerplate, its second turn asked the homeowner to inspect the 'ceramic disc' and 'metal coil' under the glass as if it were a solid-plate hob (prompting a correction), and it never asked for the model number or acknowledged the control-board possibility beyond a passing 'control switch' mention. Conversation 1's odd initial question about whether 'hob' meant software is a minor blemish that does not outweigh its substantially better diagnostic and part-advice content.
